title: Do Reviewers Still Reward Lexical Complexity? A Frozen-Rater Study of Preference Drift in 124K ICLR Reviews
abstract: arXiv:2609.08475v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models have collapsed the cost of producing lexically elaborate prose, and whether peer reviewers still reward it is a question about the evaluator, not about the text. When the association between a writing cue and review scores moves across years, the reviewers may have changed, the submissions may have changed, or both, and a regression of scores on text cannot say which. We separate the two with a frozen rater: 81,850 machine reviews of ICLR submissions from 2018 to 2025, all generated in one February-April 2025 window with one model family and one prompt, so that its year-to-year coefficients track submission composition alone and the human-minus-frozen trend difference identifies reviewer preference drift. translated_title: 审稿人还会奖励词汇复杂性吗？基于12.4万份ICLR评审的“冻结评审员”偏好漂移研究
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型已使撰写辞藻华丽的文章的成本大幅降低，而同行评审是否仍会奖励这种文风，是一个关乎评审者而非文本本身的问题。当某一写作特征与评审分数之间的关联逐年变化时，可能是评审者变了，可能是投稿变了，也可能两者皆变，而将分数对文本做回归无法区分这些情况。我们用“冻结评审员”来分离这两种效应：针对2018至2025年ICLR投稿的81,850份机器评审，全部在2025年2月至4月同一时间窗口内、用同一模型家族和同一提示词生成，因此其逐年系数仅反映投稿构成的变化，而人类评审减去冻结评审的趋势差异则可识别评审者偏好的漂移。在32,638份投稿共124,615份人类评审上，人类评审对非领域词汇复杂性的系数从+0.142降至-0.015，而冻结评审员则从+0.080变为+0.082；三重差分……
tldr: 该研究提出“冻结评审员”方法——用同一模型和提示词在固定时间窗口生成81,850份机器评审，以区分投稿构成变化与审稿人偏好变化——发现人类评审对词汇复杂性的系数从+0.142反转为-0.015而冻结评审员保持稳定，证明ICLR审稿人已真实地不再青睐辞藻华丽的写作。
en_tdlr: Using a "frozen rater" of 81,850 machine reviews generated in one fixed window with a single model family and prompt to disentangle submission composition changes from evaluator preference drift, this study shows that human reviewers' coefficient on lexical complexity flipped from +0.142 to -0.015 while the frozen rater remained stable, demonstrating genuine reviewer preference drift against lexically elaborate prose in ICLR reviews.
